beginner_version.found: Tiny separate things: yes, small rocks dotted over the left hillside and wispy cloud streaks. Textures of hundreds of items: yes, the tall grass and seed heads across the bottom third (busy outlined most of it, 13.1% of the canvas) and the cow's fur in single strands. Detail inside big shapes: yes, every hair in the fur and fringe. More parts than 8: about at the limit (sky, far hills, loch, hillside, grass, cow body, head and fringe, horns, nose).
beginner_version.list: Grass across the bottom third becomes a dark green base with loose upward flicks of olive and pale gold, no blades or seed heads; seed stalks in front of the legs become a few gold flicks; fur becomes broad curved rust and ginger strokes, darker in shadow, gold rim on the lit right and top; fringe becomes a few big curved strokes; rocks on the left hillside removed, slope becomes smooth olive with soft darker patches; wispy clouds become two or three soft streaks; far hills become three flat blue-gray bands; the loch strip stays.
beginner_version.why: At 13.1% fine texture the photo is busier than the lavender (about 10%); every step is cut from the finish, so single grass blades and hairs would land in one step. The beginner version took it to 0.2%, with the cow, horns, hills, loch and sunset light all still there.

canvas_fit.lost: about 11%: a thin strip of sky at the top and of grass at the bottom
canvas_fit.why: No --canvas given; fit-canvas picked the standard size closest to the 2:3 photo, and a crop keeps the whole cow, both horns and the grass.

photo_prep.subject: A shaggy ginger Highland cow with long upturned horns standing in tall grass on a moor at sunset, backlit from the upper right, with hills, a sliver of loch, and a pale gold sky behind.
photo_prep.why: No bars, borders, captions, watermarks, or unrelated scene around the subject; the whole image is the picture.

considered.name: Block in, then build up
considered.why_not: It has no version 2 keys (v2_step_range, v2_rules), so pipeline v2 can't plan from it; the owner also picked paint-along for acrylic beginners.

technique.why: Paint along, back to front is the only whole-painting approach with version 2 keys, and it fits: a sky, far hills, a near hillside, then the cow and grass in front, painted farthest to nearest on a white canvas.
